what_is_it.summary: The OpenAI Agents SDK is a lightweight, production-ready Python framework for building multi-agent AI workflows. It provides a small set of powerful primitives — Agents, Handoffs, Guardrails, and Tracing — that enable developers to build complex agentic applications without a steep learning curve.
what_is_it.tagline: A lightweight, powerful framework for multi-agent workflows

predecessor.name: Swarm
predecessor.description: Educational framework exploring ergonomic, lightweight multi-agent orchestration
predecessor.note: Swarm was an experimental project by the OpenAI Solutions team. The Agents SDK is its production-ready upgrade.

release_history.development_pace: Very active — averaging multiple releases per week

key_features.description: Built-in agent loop that handles tool invocation, sends results back to the LLM, and continues until the task is complete.
Use built-in language features to orchestrate and chain agents, rather than needing to learn new abstractions.
Powerful mechanism for coordinating and delegating work across multiple agents. Handoffs are represented as tools to the LLM, enabling dynamic task routing.
Run specialists inside real isolated workspaces with manifest-defined files, sandbox client choice (Unix local, Docker, hosted), and resumable sandbox sessions.

Run input validation and safety checks in parallel with agent execution (or blocking). Supports input guardrails (first agent), output guardrails (final output), and tool guardrails (per-tool-call). Tripwire mechanism for fast failure.
Turn any Python function into a tool with automatic schema generation and Pydantic-powered validation.
Built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server tool integration that works the same way as function tools.
Persistent memory layer for maintaining working context within an agent loop. Supports SQLAlchemy, SQLite, Redis, MongoDB, Dapr, and encrypted backends.
Built-in mechanisms for involving humans across agent runs.

Built-in tracing for visualizing, debugging, and monitoring workflows. Collects LLM generations, tool calls, handoffs, guardrails, and custom events. Integrates with OpenAI's evaluation, fine-tuning, and distillation tools.
Build powerful voice agents with gpt-realtime-2.1, automatic interruption detection, context management, and guardrails over WebSocket connections.
Supports OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions APIs, plus 100+ other LLMs through multi-provider support.
Build voice-enabled agents with speech-to-text and text-to-speech capabilities, with automatic transcription and speech spans in tracing.

Agent.definition: An LLM configured with instructions, tools, guardrails, handoffs, and optional structured output types.
Agent.code_example: agent = Agent(name='Haiku agent', instructions='Always respond in haiku form', model='gpt-5-nano', tools=[get_weather])

Handoff.definition: Mechanism allowing an agent to delegate tasks to another specialist agent. Handoffs are represented as tools to the LLM.
key_features: Custom tool name and description overrides
input_type for structured data from LLM at handoff time
input_filter for filtering conversation history passed to next agent

types.input_guardrails: Run on the first user input for the agent chain. Supports parallel (default, better latency) and blocking (cost-saving) execution modes.
types.output_guardrails: Run on the final agent output. Always runs after agent completes.
types.tool_guardrails: Wrap function tools — validate/block tool calls before and after execution. Input checks before execution, output checks after.

Guardrails.mechanism: Guardrail function → GuardrailFunctionOutput → check tripwire_triggered → raise InputGuardrailTripwireTriggered or OutputGuardrailTripwireTriggered

Tracing.definition: Built-in observability system collecting comprehensive records of agent runs.
Tracing.hierarchy: Trace (end-to-end workflow) → Spans (operations with start/end times)
Tracing.default_behavior: Enabled by default. Can disable globally (env var), per-run, or via ZDR policy.
Tracing.export: BatchTraceProcessor exports every few seconds; flush_traces() for immediate delivery in workers (Celery, FastAPI background tasks).

Runner.definition: Orchestrates agent execution — manages turns, tool calls, guardrails, handoffs, and sessions.
Runner.vs_direct_api: Use Runner for managed workflows; use Responses API directly when you want to own the loop yourself.

SandboxAgent.definition: Agent preconfigured to run inside an isolated workspace with manifest-defined files and sandbox-native capabilities.

use_sdk_when: You want the runtime to manage turns, tool execution, guardrails, handoffs, or sessions
Your agent should produce artifacts or operate across multiple coordinated steps
You need a real workspace or resumable execution through Sandbox agents
use_api_directly_when: You want to own the loop, tool dispatch, and state handling yourself
Your workflow is short-lived and mainly about returning the model's response

openai_api_relationship.ecosystem_integration: Tracing integrates with OpenAI suite of evaluation, fine-tuning, and distillation tools. Prompt templates can reference prompts created in the OpenAI Platform playground.

vs_LangGraph.langgraph: General-purpose graph-based agent framework by LangChain. Uses StateGraph with nodes and edges for complex, branching workflows.
vs_LangGraph.agents_sdk: Simpler, fewer abstractions. Agent-centric (not graph-centric). Opinionated about the agent loop. Easier to learn but less flexible for arbitrary graph topologies.
vs_LangGraph.key_difference: Philosophy: Agents SDK prioritizes simplicity and quick learning curve; LangGraph prioritizes maximum control and composability.

vs_CrewAI.crewai: Role-based multi-agent framework where agents have defined roles, goals, and backstories. Focuses on collaborative task execution with sequential or hierarchical processes.
vs_CrewAI.agents_sdk: Lighter weight with fewer abstractions. No built-in role/backstory concepts. Handoffs provide similar multi-agent coordination but more programmatic.
vs_CrewAI.key_difference: CrewAI is more opinionated about agent roles and collaboration patterns; Agents SDK is more flexible and lower-level.

vs_AutoGen.autogen: Microsoft's multi-agent conversation framework supporting diverse conversation patterns, code execution, and human-in-the-loop. Originally multi-backend (now more OpenAI-focused).
vs_AutoGen.agents_sdk: More OpenAI-native. Simpler API surface. Built-in tracing and guardrails that AutoGen provides through separate mechanisms.
vs_AutoGen.key_difference: AutoGen provides richer conversation patterns (group chat, nested chat); Agents SDK is more streamlined with a focus on handoffs and a cleaner API.

vs_Swarm_predecessor.swarm: Experimental educational framework. Lightweight but not production-hardened. No built-in tracing, guardrails, or session management.
vs_Swarm_predecessor.agents_sdk: Production-ready upgrade. Adds tracing, guardrails, sessions, sandbox agents, realtime agents, MCP support, and multi-provider support.

installation: pip install openai-agents  (voice: pip install 'openai-agents[voice]', redis sessions: pip install 'openai-agents[redis]', docker sandbox: pip install 'openai-agents[docker]')
design_principles: Enough features to be worth using, but few enough primitives to make it quick to learn
Works great out of the box, but you can customize exactly what happens
